title: History and Evolution of Bash knowledge check

questions.prompt: Which topic is explicitly listed under “History and Evolution of Bash”?
options: What Bash is and what it does
Bash as a shell and scripting language
questions.explanation: The supplied Bash.pdf curriculum lists “Origins of Bash” under lesson 3, “History and Evolution of Bash”. Review the topic in the lesson content to connect the term with its practical use.

questions.prompt: Which approach is the strongest default when applying “History and Evolution of Bash”?
options: Evaluate constructed user-controlled strings as shell commands to reduce parsing code.
Skip version checks because all common environments provide the same Bash features.
Bash reads and executes shell commands; its expansions and external programs have distinct behavior.
Assume that a working happy-path example proves correctness for every input.
questions.answer_key: Bash reads and executes shell commands; its expansions and external programs have distinct behavior.
questions.explanation: Bash reads and executes shell commands; its expansions and external programs have distinct behavior. This approach keeps assumptions visible and makes results verifiable.

questions.prompt: Which practice best prevents a common reliability or maintenance error related to “History and Evolution of Bash”?
options: Assume the command behaves the same across all versions and operating systems.
Skip invalid inputs because the example uses trusted sample data.
Treat one successful output as proof that the workflow is safe in production.
Use a small reproducible example, test an edge case, and record both the result and an important limitation.
questions.answer_key: Use a small reproducible example, test an edge case, and record both the result and an important limitation.
questions.explanation: Use a small reproducible example, test an edge case, and record both the result and an important limitation. The appropriate checks depend on the target environment and should be reviewed before publishing a script.
